subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access-deny boundary for that skill directory, or should hard isolation use a separate explicit security policy?
rationale: Current source makes the reported gap clear, but changing `enabled` semantics crosses public config, security, sandbox, exec, UI, and upgrade expectations that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
options.body: Treat `enabled: false` as a security-facing deny state and implement centralized read, exec, and sandbox enforcement for disabled skill directories.

options.title: Add a separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled: false` as eligibility-only and introduce a clearly named operator-controlled policy for hard skill filesystem and exec isolation.

options.title: Document non-boundary semantics
options.body: If hard isolation is out of scope, document that disabling only affects matching and visibility, then route deployments to sandbox, tool denial, or filesystem isolation controls.

recommendation.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled: false` as a security-facing deny state and implement centralized read, exec, and sandbox enforcement for disabled skill directories.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily a security/product boundary choice, and the history points to adjacent skill hardening work by this owner.
